Mesillat Yesharim 11:54: And their particulars are numerous, as numerous as all their known laws set forth in the books of the decisors. And whoever is lenient with them where they said to be stringent is nothing but a destroyer of his own soul. And so they said (Sifra, Shemini): "you shall not defile yourselves through them, lest you become defiled through them" (Leviticus 11:43) — if you defile yourselves through them, in the end you will become defiled through them.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:55: That is, forbidden foods introduce impurity into a person's heart and soul until the holiness of the Omnipresent, blessed be He, withdraws and grows distant from him. This is what they also said in the Talmud (Yoma 39a): "lest you become defiled" — do not read it "ve-nitmeitem," but "ve-nitamtem" [you shall become dulled].
Mesillat Yesharim 11:56: For transgression dulls a person's heart, for it removes from him true understanding and the spirit of intellect that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives to the pious, as Scripture says (Proverbs 2:6): "For the Lord gives wisdom" — and he remains beastlike and material, sunk in the coarseness of this world.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:57: And forbidden foods surpass all other prohibitions in this respect, since they enter into a person's body itself and become flesh of his flesh. And in order to inform us that not only unclean animals or repugnant creatures are the impure ones, but even the non-kosher members of the kosher species itself are included in impurity, Scripture says (Leviticus 11:47): "to distinguish between the unclean and the clean."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:58: And the explanation came from our Sages, of blessed memory (Torat Kohanim): There is no need to say "between a donkey and a cow" — why, then, does it say "between the unclean and the clean"? Between what is unclean for you and what is clean for you — between an animal whose windpipe was slaughtered through the greater part, and one slaughtered through half of it. And how much is there between the greater part and half? A hairsbreadth. So far their words.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:59: And they said these words at the conclusion of their statement — "and how much is there between the greater part, etc." — to show how wondrous is the power of the commandment, that a hairsbreadth actually separates impurity from purity.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:60: Now, whoever has any sense in his head should regard forbidden foods as poisonous foods, or as food into which some poisonous substance has become mixed. For if such a thing were to happen, would a person go easy on himself and eat from it?
Mesillat Yesharim 11:61: If any concern at all remained for him — even a small suspicion — would he not certainly refrain? And certainly he would not be lenient. And if he were lenient, he would be considered nothing but an utter fool.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:62: So too with forbidden food, we have already explained that it is actual poison for the heart and the soul. If so, then, who would be lenient in a case of doubtful prohibition, if he has any sense at all? And concerning this it is said (Proverbs 23:2): "and put a knife to your throat, if you are a man of appetite."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:63: Let us now speak of the common sins that arise from human society and interaction, such as misrepresentation in words, shaming someone to their face, misleading the blind with advice, gossip, hatred and vengeance, oaths, falsehood, and desecration of God's Name — for who could say, I am clean of these, I am pure of guilt in them? For their branches are numerous and exceedingly fine, so that being careful of them is a great labor.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:64: Misrepresentation in words includes speaking to one's fellow alone in a manner that would shame him — all the more so speaking in front of many people something that would shame him — or doing something to him that would cause him shame.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:65: This is what they said in the chapter "Ha-Zahav" (Bava Metzia 58b): if he was a penitent, one should not say to him, "Remember your former deeds," etc. If afflictions came upon him, one should not say to him, as his friends said to Job (Job 4:7): "Remember, I pray you, who ever perished being innocent, etc." If donkey-drivers were seeking grain from him, one should not say to them, "Go to so-and-so, who sells grain," knowing that he never sold grain in his life.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:66: And they have already said, of blessed memory (ibid.): the misrepresentation of words is worse than the misrepresentation of money, etc. And all the more so if it is done in public, for we learned explicitly (Avot 3:15): whoever shames his fellow's face in public has no share in the World to Come. And Rav Chisda said (Bava Metzia 59a): all the gates of prayer are locked, except the gates of misrepresentation. And Rabbi Elazar said: for everything, the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment through an agent, except for misrepresentation.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:67: And they said: there are three for whom the Curtain before the Divine Throne is never locked, and one of them is misrepresentation. And even for a matter of a commandment, Scripture says (Leviticus 19:17): "you shall surely rebuke your fellow," and they said, of blessed memory (Arachin 16b): one might think, even if his face changes color from shame? Therefore Scripture says, "and you shall not bear sin because of him."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:68: From all these statements you will see how far the branches of this warning extend, and how severe its punishment is.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:69: Regarding the giving of advice, we learned in Torat Kohanim (Leviticus 19): "and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block" — before one who is blind in the matter. If he asks you, "What is the status of so-and-so's daughter for marriage into the priesthood?" do not tell him she is fit when she is in fact unfit. If he sought advice from you, do not give him advice that is unsuitable for him, etc.; and do not tell him, "Sell your field and buy yourself a donkey," while you circumvent him and take it from him yourself. Should you say, "I am giving him good advice" — behold, the matter is left to the heart, as it is said, "and you shall fear your God."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:70: We thus learn that whether in a matter in which he might have a personal interest, or in a matter in which he has no interest at all, a person is obligated to present to one who comes to consult him the pure and clear truth.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:71: And you will see that the Torah anticipated the ultimate intention of deceivers — for we are not dealing with fools, who would give advice whose evil is publicly known and revealed, but with those who are clever in doing evil, who give advice to their fellows which, on its face, appears to genuinely benefit their fellow, but whose ultimate purpose is not for their fellow's good but for his harm and for the advisor's own benefit. Therefore they said, "should you say, I am giving good advice, etc., behold, the matter is left to the heart, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:72: And how many people stumble in these sins day after day, being drawn and carried along by the force of their desire for gain! And the gravity of their punishment has already been made clear in Scripture (Deuteronomy 27:18): "Cursed be he who causes the blind to go astray on the road."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:73: But this is the obligation of the upright person: when a person comes to consult him, he should give him the very advice that he would take for himself, without any consideration except the benefit of the one seeking advice, and no other purpose whatsoever, near or far.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:74: And should it happen that he sees harm to himself in that advice, if he can point this out to the face of the one seeking advice, he should point it out. And if not, he should withdraw from the matter and not advise him. But in any case, he should not give him advice whose purpose is anything other than the benefit of the one seeking advice — unless the intention of the one seeking advice is for evil, in which case it is certainly a mitzvah to deceive him, as it is already said (Psalms 18:27): "and with the crooked You show Yourself subtle," as Chushai the Archite demonstrates.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:75: As for gossip and evil speech, their gravity is already known, and the extent of their branches, for they are very numerous, to the point that our Sages, of blessed memory, have already decreed, in the statement I have already mentioned (Bava Batra 165a): "and all of them in the dust of evil speech."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:76: And they said (Arachin 15b): what is an example of evil speech? Such as saying, "Where can fire be found except in so-and-so's house" — or telling someone's praises before his enemies, and the like — for even though these things appear light and far removed from gossip, they are in truth part of its dust.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:77: The general rule of the matter is: the inclination has many paths. But anything that could give rise to harm or disgrace to one's fellow, whether in his presence or not in his presence, is included in the category of evil speech, which is hated and abominated before the Omnipresent, concerning which they said (ibid.): whoever tells evil speech is as though he denied the fundamental principle of faith; and Scripture says explicitly (Psalms 101:5): "Whoever slanders his fellow in secret, him will I destroy."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:78: Hatred and vengeance are also very difficult for the deceived heart of man to escape, for a person feels his humiliations very keenly and suffers great pain from them, and revenge is sweeter than honey to him, for it alone is his solace.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:79: Therefore, for a person to have the strength to abandon what his nature compels him to, and to go against his own traits — neither to hate one who has aroused hatred in him, nor to take revenge upon him when the opportunity to do so presents itself, nor to bear him a grudge, but rather to forget it all and remove it from his heart as though it had never been — this is strong and mighty indeed.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:80: And this is easy only for the ministering angels, in whom these traits do not exist, not for those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust. However, it is the decree of the King, and the verses are plainly and clearly stated, needing no explanation: "You shall not hate your brother in your heart" (Leviticus 19:17); "You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people" (ibid. 19:18).
Mesillat Yesharim 11:81: And the matter of vengeance and grudge-bearing is well known, namely:
Mesillat Yesharim 11:82: Vengeance — refraining from doing good to one who did not wish to do good to you, or who has already done you harm.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:83: Grudge-bearing — to mention, at the time one is doing good to one who has harmed him, some memory of the harm he did to him.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:84: For since the inclination continually inflames the heart and constantly seeks to leave at least some impression or some memory of the matter — and if it cannot leave a large memory, it will strive to leave a small one — it says, by way of example, to a person: If you wish to give this man what he was unwilling to give you when you needed it, at least do not give it to him with a pleasant countenance; or if you do not wish to do him harm, at least do not do him a great good, nor give him great assistance; or if you do wish to help him greatly, at least do not do it in his presence, or do not resume associating with him and being his friend — if you have forgiven him so that you no longer appear to him as an enemy, that is enough — and even if you do wish to associate with him, at least do not show him as much affection as before.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:85: And so with all similar things — the various kinds of cunning of the inclination, by which it strives to entice the hearts of men. Therefore the Torah came and formulated a general principle that encompasses everything (Leviticus 19:18): "and you shall love your fellow as yourself" — "as yourself" with no distinction at all, "as yourself" with no divisions, without stratagems or schemes — literally, as yourself.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:86: As for oaths — although, as a matter of course, anyone who is not among the uncultivated guards himself from taking the Name of Heaven in vain in speech, all the more so in an oath — there are still some minor branches which, although not among the more severe matters, are nonetheless proper for one who wishes to be clean to guard against.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:87: This is what they said (Shevuot 36a): Rabbi Elazar said, saying "No" can be an oath, and "Yes" can be an oath. Rava said: this is when he said "No, no" twice, or said "Yes, yes" twice.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:88: And so they said (Bava Metzia 49a): "and a righteous hin" (Leviticus 19:36) — that your "no" be righteous and your "yes" be righteous.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:89: Now, falsehood is also a grievous illness that has spread widely among mankind, and yet there are levels within it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:90: There are people whose very profession is falsehood itself: they go about fabricating from their own hearts complete falsehoods, in order to increase conversation among people or to be considered wise and knowledgeable about many things; and of them it is said (Proverbs 12:22): "Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord." And it says (Isaiah 59:3): "your lips have spoken lies, your tongue mutters wickedness." And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already decreed (Sotah 42a): four groups do not receive the presence of the Divine Presence, and one of them is the group of liars.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:91: And there are others close to them in level, although not exactly like them, and these are those who falsify in their stories and their words — that is, their profession is not to go about fabricating stories and events that never occurred and never will occur; but when they come to tell of something, they mix in falsehoods as it occurs to their spirit, and they become so accustomed to this that it becomes for them like a second nature — and these are the habitual liars, whose words cannot be believed, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 89b): such is the punishment of the habitual liar — that even when he speaks the truth, he is not listened to, for this evil has already become so ingrained in them that their words cannot come forth from their mouths free of falsehood. This is what the prophet laments and says (Jeremiah 9:4): "They have taught their tongue to speak lies; they weary themselves to commit iniquity."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:92: And there are yet others whose illness is milder than that of the first ones — those who are not so fixed in falsehood, but simply do not take care to distance themselves from it; and if the occasion arises, they will say it, and many times they will say it in jest or the like, without evil intent.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:93: However, the wise man has informed us that all this is contrary to the will of the Creator, blessed be He, and to the character of His pious ones. This is what is written (Proverbs 13:5): "A righteous man hates falsehood." And this is what the warning concerns (Exodus 23:7): "from a false matter you shall distance yourself." And you will see that it does not say "from falsehood you shall guard yourself," but "from a false matter you shall distance yourself," to alert us to the great distance and extensive flight required to flee from this. And it has already been said (Zephaniah 3:13): "The remnant of Israel shall do no wrong, and shall not speak lies, neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth."
